comment: The DeepSeek Harness version line this plugin pack is built and tested against. Plugins are shipped as alpha until the owner promotes them to stable. The installer pins this exact dsh version when driving the CLI. 'vendoredFrom' records the harness line whose client bundles dsh-rightbar / dsh-rightbar-files / dsh-open-in-app were forked from. dsh-vn-master is the pack's master: the bundle layer alone - the pack's final word per row, no browser half.
comment_platforms: The plugins are plain JavaScript and platform-neutral; the only OS-specific code is a launcher choosing the right command for the host: dsh-open-in-app's file-browser launcher (explorer.exe / open / xdg-open, WSL-aware), the run launcher's browser hand-off (Chrome on PATH / the standard install folders / the App Paths registry entry, 'open -a Google Chrome', google-chrome or chromium, else the platform default). The launchers run on Windows (install.bat / uninstall.bat, PowerShell 5.1 or 7, and the run launcher: the double-clickable batch run-web.bat at the root plus its worker scripts/run-web.ps1, because cmd's for /f reads a child's output only up to EOF and cannot watch a running harness) and on macOS/Linux (install.sh / uninstall.sh / run-web.sh, POSIX sh - never PowerShell). The run launcher is run-web.bat + run-web.sh at the repo root, and run-web.sh does the whole job itself. The ready URL reaches the browser as ONE ARGV ELEMENT - Start-Process -ArgumentList on Windows, an argument of open/xdg-open on macOS/Linux - never through a command string.

dsh-vn-master.role: the pack's master: the bundle layer alone (installed last, so it is the final word per row), with no dsh.client, no service, no inject edge and no code. What it carries is the pack's statements about shipped ROWS, in two kinds. A ROW RESTATEMENT belongs here when a row a package REPLACES is not involved, and alpha.2 is the first: `ui-sidebar-browser` -> `disabled: false`, because 0.2 declares the right Sidebar's Browser tab desktop-only while this pack targets the raw web profile, and a later layer wins per row - the browser package then registers its own tab type AND its own guide entry into the sidebarRightTabs registry, so the Start page lists the Browser by itself and no pack code draws it. A pack-wide PRODUCT DECISION belongs here too, and alpha.3 is the first: the feedback surface is REMOVED, because vncode is its own product and does not ask its users for feedback - the shipped dialog says in its own words that a submission includes the current conversation log, and that submission is exactly what releases an upload to a third party. Four rows go: `ui-message-feedback` (the Like/Dislike action strip, the Submit-feedback dialog and its toast, the `/feedback` composer decoration and the feedbackUi service), `message-feedback` and `command-feedback` (the two host halves - the messageFeedback / sessionFeedback Remotes and the log-only feedback events they append) and `session-telemetry-otel` (the FEEDBACK_ONLY export path: it captures a Session-log prefix and ships it to https://dsh-otel-collector.deepseeksvc.com/v1/logs with the anonymous user id once a feedback event exists, so removing the producers leaves it nothing to release and disabling the row - the launcher's OWN privacy switch, the same `disabled: true` a non-empty DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED resolves to - means the exporter is never constructed). Nothing else consumes those services; the shipped Session export guards its entry as ctx.get('feedbackUi')?.openSession(...), so /export keeps working. A disable that belongs to the package REPLACING a row still stays with that package (dsh-rightbar's ui-sidebar-right / ui-sidebar-files), so a partial install still mounts one bar. The account menu's own hardcoded Feedback item is not a row and is not disabled here: dsh-themes hides it, and a `config` override of its contactFormUrl was rejected on purpose because a row with `volatile` fields has its whole config replaced by the next volatile write from a settings form, which would take the override with it

dsh-rightbar.role: the pack's right bar, forked from the shipped bundle and patched by scripts/sync-vendored.ps1. Its eleven patches do four things, and all four are needed. First, the dock's TWO-pane cap is lifted in the five places the core bundle enforces it (the split intent, the edge-drop intent, the surface's canSplit prop, the split command) and the top/bottom drop bands are re-opened ('Add top split' / 'Add bottom split' were already in the core locales and glyphs), so the ceiling is the docking kit's own canSplit: four docked panes, with the disabled-hint label in both languages naming that ceiling. That alone is not enough, because the kit DRAWS that layout with the wrong component: DockLayout renders one pane or two side by side and THROWS on anything else (DockLayout requires one pane or two horizontally split panes), so a stacked pane - and with it the 2x2 the top/bottom bands exist for - reached the shell's slot boundary as a crash, and an abdicated slot entry took the whole bar away until a page reload. The last two patches render the kit's own recursive DockSurface instead (the same drop-zone host: splitRow/splitColumn, a divider per child, one strip per pane) and splice in the wrapper that keeps what the flat renderer gave for free: the data-dockkit-host='dock' box the bar's own stylesheet hides and slides the docked content with; pointer-events:auto on it, because that stylesheet turns the PANEL's pointer events off and the flat renderer's per-tab hosts were what turned them back on (without it the bar is deaf to the mouse); the kit's FloatLayer, because the flat renderer drew a floated tab as a grid cell and the surface renderer draws none; the active/expanded gates, so an off-screen panel or a collapsed bar mounts no tabs; and keepMounted, so a retained tab stays mounted once it has been in front. That wrapper is packages/dsh-rightbar/vendor/dock-tree.js - the package's one hand-written file, spliced in verbatim by the sync script and pinned byte-for-byte against the fork by the tracked check. The 2x2 is built by dragging a tab into a pane's top or bottom quarter (right band first for the column, then the left pane's top band, then the right pane's bottom band; a drag must not empty its pane, since the kit merges an empty one away), and floating panels were never counted, so they remain the way past four. Every claim above was measured in headless Edge against the real app with real pointer input: four tabs, three drags, four panes of 304x428 in a 2x2, no slot error at any point, the collapse round trip hiding and restoring all four, and a floated tab docking back. The sync script also refuses to build the fork from anything but the PINNED line now, because this machine carries 0.1.5-rc.1 beside 0.2.0-rc.2 and the older line's bundle is a different shape entirely. Nothing else in the fork differs from core - no contract, slot or service change. ALPHA.4 restores the bar's LEFT SEAM, the hairline that divides it from the centre column, which the renderer swap above had taken away with the two-pane cap: the kit draws that line as a left border on the column-0 TAB CELL (._tabCell_<hash>[data-dockkit-host=dock][data-dockkit-column="0"]>._tabHost_<hash>), and that markup is the FLAT renderer's own - DockSurface draws a bare _pane_ section carrying NEITHER attribute - so once the fork rendered the surface the selector matched nothing and the bar and the centre column, both --dsw-alias-bg-base, ran together with nothing between them. DockTree's wrapper already re-emits data-dockkit-host="dock" on a real box (the bar's own stylesheet slides and hides the docked content through it), so the seam is drawn there on --dsw-alias-border-l3 - the token the app's OWN column separators use (the left sidebar's border-right, and the centre column's border-left under [data-platform=darwin]) - while the kit's cell rule asked for the stronger -l4, because the two sides of the frame should wear the same hairline. ALPHA.5 gives the same wrapper the other thing the flat renderer's tab host provided - an OPAQUE --dsw-alias-bg-base FILL - and it is the fix for a bug that only ever appeared in FULLSCREEN: the kit's background rule is ._tabHost_:not(._float_){background:var(--dsw-alias-bg-base)}, which is again markup only the FLAT renderer emits, so a surface-rendered bar has NO surface of its own. In push mode nobody can tell (the bar's column and the centre column are the same colour); in fullscreen the panel overlays the conversation, which it is NOT the same colour as, so every pixel the active tab does not paint itself shows the chat through it - and WHICH tab is in front decides how bad it looks, because the editor and the PDF viewer paint their own background while the History tab (its rail, its commit list, its diff detail) paints none, which is why it read as a tab that "sometimes does not cover" and looked like it needed a refresh. Nothing was stale: the fill goes on the box the tab bodies are MOUNTED IN, so it cannot be defeated by a tab that paints nothing and no future tab can punch a hole in the bar again. Three properties keep the pair safe: both live on panelBody's FIRST child and the flat fallback renders no such box, so neither can double the kit's own declarations; both ride the [data-sidebar-right-open] gate the stylesheet puts on that box, so a COLLAPSED bar carries the fill and the seam off-screen with its content instead of painting a one-bar-wide rectangle over the conversation; and both are recorded patches rather than hand edits, pinned from both sides by the tracked client check (the declarations in the fork, and the label a re-sync rebuilds them from). ALPHA.6 is the LAYER, and the reason an opaque fill was still not enough: .P3OORG_panel is position:absolute and leaves z-index at auto, so it paints above the chat's in-flow content and UNDER every positioned element the app gives a positive z-index - measured from the pinned line's own bundles, the composer seat is position:sticky; bottom:0; z-index:7 (9 with a trigger menu open) on a gradient that fades to transparent over its top 36px, its width handle is 8 and its workspace row 10, the frame's column resize handles are 11, its leading seat 15 and its overlay layer 20, this pack's own command dock (dsh-cmdbar) is position:fixed; bottom:0; z-index:21, and the sidebar's fixed controls are 30 under [data-windows-titlebar]. The kit had already answered that for the FLAT renderer: the fullscreen panel sets --dsh-dockkit-dock-layer:40 against 10 when pushed, and that is the z-index of its tab CELLS, ordered in the root stacking context because the panel creates none - and DockSurface draws no tab cell, so the surface path lost that layer too and a fullscreen bar sat under the composer, the header seats and the sidebar while the chat's text showed through the composer's own gradient. The layer now goes on the PANEL (.P3OORG_panel[data-sidebar-right-panel=fullscreen]{--dsh-dockkit-dock-layer:40;z-index:40}), which restores the intent and covers what the cells never could: the bar's own fill, and the float layer, since floats are children of the panel and stay inside its stacking context, keeping the kit's own float-above-dock relation rather than being stranded under the bar. 40 is taken from the ladder rather than invented - above everything persistent (a maximum of 30) and below every transient layer (the kit's tab menu 70, tooltips and panel menus 100, submenus 101, the modal root and its backdrops 1000, toasts and portals 1100) - so dropdowns, menus, dialogs and toasts still win, which 'the bar is on top' must not break; and it is stated as a consequence that the pack's OWN command dock (21) is covered by a fullscreen bar too, so if the dock should survive one, that is dsh-cmdbar's number to raise above 40. PUSH mode is deliberately untouched: upstream's pushed dock layer is 10, below the shell's own 11/15/20 chrome, and the two columns do not overlap there. The tracked check reads the pinned layout and sidebar bundles back and asserts the bar's layer is above the highest z-index they declare, so a harness bump that moves the ladder fails the check instead of shipping a bar under the input box.

dsh-editor.role: the editable text/code tab type (kind `editor`): CodeMirror 6 in the right bar's pane, Markdown included, blank documents created through the + control, and a Preview hand-off to the shipped rendered view. Its toolbar is the tab's own TOP BAR (alpha.9): 38px with box-sizing:border-box, the same box the shipped Files tab and the document preview use, so the pane's first hairline lands on the y=76 line the 38px docking strip, the conversation header (min-height:76px) and the left column's branding band all end on - it was 42.5px (8px padding around a 26px control) and sat ~4.5px low. ALPHA.10 adds the SHELL LANGUAGES: .sh/.bash/.zsh/.ksh/.dash, .ps1/.psm1/.psd1 and .bat/.cmd opened with NO language at all - one flat colour, and in the light theme the same colour as everything else - because the map stopped at yaml and CodeMirror has no Lezer parser for any of the three. They ride on StreamLanguage: the vendored bundle (rebuilt) now carries `shell` and `powerShell` from @codemirror/legacy-modes, and because CM5 and CM6 both never shipped a batch mode this pack supplies one as a vendor build input (vendor/batch-mode.js, CM5-style token names - the vocabulary StreamLanguage maps onto the highlight tags defaultHighlightStyle and oneDark already colour) that knows @echo off, rem/:: comments, labels, %VAR% and %~dp0 expansions, /switches and the variable a `set` names. ALPHA.11 adds RUST AND TOML: .rs and .toml opened with no language at all for exactly the same reason, and they take the same route - neither has a Lezer parser among the packages vendored here (@codemirror/lang-rust is a separate package and CM6 ships no official TOML grammar at all) while @codemirror/legacy-modes carries a ported CM5 mode for BOTH, so the rebuilt bundle gains `rust` (a simpleMode: keywords and the name a fn/struct/enum/type/union declares, primitive types and true/false/Some/None/Ok/Err, char and byte literals, all four string spellings, numeric literals with their suffixes and bases, #[attributes], //, /* */ and macro names) and `toml` (the hand-written stream parser: [table] and [[array of tables]] headers, the key on the left of an `=`, strings in all four quote spellings, `#` comments, dates, booleans, arrays and numbers), and lib/client.js maps rs -> CM.rust and toml -> CM.toml through the same StreamLanguage.define() call - so the same defaultHighlightStyle (light) and oneDark (dark) that colour a .js colour them too. ALPHA.12 fixes the one bug alpha.11 shipped, and it was an engine/bundle VERSION SKEW: the vendored engine is ONE generated artifact at ONE stable URL, it was cached in memory for the life of the harness process and served with cache-control public, max-age=3600, so opening a .rs tab after the upgrade ran a NEW client bundle against the OLD engine - and StreamLanguage.define(undefined) dereferences the mode it is handed, which killed the whole tab with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading languageData)'. Four changes, one per half of the mismatch: the engine request is VERSION-QUALIFIED (/api/dsh-editor/vendor?v=<bundle version>, the route matching on pathname so the query is free), the route answers cache-control: no-cache instead of a freshness window (the ETag is the content hash, so revalidation is a 304 and never a re-download), the route re-stats the artifact per request and re-reads it when the stamp changed so a rebuild needs no harness restart (a missing file never discards a good copy), and a mode the loaded engine does not carry degrades to NO LANGUAGE with one console warning naming the skew - a document that opens unhighlighted beats a dead tab. The tracked checks pin all four (the client check asserts the single wrapping call site, the version-qualified URL and the absence of any direct StreamLanguage.define(CM.x); the route check asserts no-cache, the content-hash ETag shape, the 304, HEAD without a body, and that the served bytes really carry every mode the client names). ALPHA.13 closes the half alpha.12 left open: the guard covered the five STREAM modes and left the seven LEZER ones called straight off the engine (CM.javascript(), CM.json(), CM.markdown(), CM.python(), CM.html(), CM.css(), CM.yaml()), so a bundle newer than its artifact answered 'CM.yaml is not a function' and openFile's catch turned that into the very 'Editor unavailable' tab the fix exists to prevent - the README's claim was broader than the code. Two lookups now serve the two families, because the engine answers in two SHAPES: engineLanguage(CM, name) wants a Lezer factory (a function) and engineStreamMode(CM, name) wants the StreamParser OBJECT a legacy mode is, which carries token() and is therefore found by an object test - the shape alpha.13's first cut missed, one function-only lookup being exactly what broke the two modes alpha.11 had just added. Each returns null and reports once when the engine exports nothing of that name, lezerLanguage builds through the first and streamLanguage through the second, and languageExtensionFor therefore contains NO direct CM.<name>(...) call at all (the tracked check FAILS on a bare `return CM.<name>(` reappearing, which is how a future mapping would add the bug back, and separately pins that the stream modes are looked up as OBJECTS rather than factories). The warning's remedy was stale as well - it still said the route 'caches the artifact in memory for the life of the harness process, so RESTART dsh web', which alpha.12 had just made false: a restart cannot help when the artifact ON DISK is the old one - so it now names the REBUILD command (packages/dsh-editor/vendor: npx --yes esbuild entry.js --bundle --minify --format=iife --global-name=DSHEditorCM --target=es2020 --outfile=../lib/vendor/cm6.min.js) and says a restart is neither needed nor useful. The check pins the guard shape, the rebuild wording, the absence of the old restart wording, the Lezer factories really being carried by the artifact, and PLUGIN_VERSION equalling package.json's version - the qualifier is only worth anything while those two agree, and alpha.10 shipped a client whose constant said alpha.9

shadowsSlots.why: the rendered Markdown body carries the Edit toggle back into the editor (lower priority renders) and undoes what the preview's plain-text scrollport imposes on its contents (white-space:pre and the mono font stack)

dsh-gittree.role: the workspace's COMMIT HISTORY as a page tab type, labelled History in the capsule and the chip while the package, row and address keep the gittree name (guide order 30, after Files and Editor), with the branch and current commit in its file bar; its Node half owns read-only /api/dsh-gittree routes, and the tab reads state with brief=1 so no file list is ever built - no fork, no core row disabled, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track. Its toolbar is the tab's own TOP BAR (alpha.4): 38px with box-sizing:border-box, the same box the shipped Files tab and the document preview use, so the pane's first hairline lands on the y=76 line the 38px docking strip, the conversation header (min-height:76px) and the left column's branding band all end on - it was 42.5px (8px padding around a 26px control) and sat ~4.5px low. ALPHA.5 draws the GRAPH: every history row sits beside a rail - a vertical rectangle on the left of the list carrying one column per branch lane, a node per commit, the line running up to the newer commit above it, and the curves where a branch leaves a merge or rejoins the line - laid out by one forward pass over `git log` in its own order (children before parents), from the parents the history route now carries as `%P` plus the ref decorations as `%D`. A merge wears a hollow node and a `#N` pull-request chip when the commit names one (GitHub's "Merge pull request #12 from ...", a "(#12)" squash subject, or a `refs/pull/12/...` ref a repository fetched), and the branch HEAD points at / a tag / a remote wears a ref chip. Nothing is measured: a row is exactly 28px and every coordinate comes from the lane index, so the rail runs straight through an expanded commit's detail with no ResizeObserver

dsh-image.role: images as a surface (row `image`, tab kind `image`): PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, BMP, ICO, SVG and TIFF open in a viewer that FITS the pane, zooms on a ladder (5%-800%) with fit-to-pane and 100%-actual-pixels, wheel-zooms at the pointer with Ctrl/Cmd, and is dragged to pan with a grab cursor MEASURED from real overflow. The zoom moves the LAYOUT (a box sized naturalPixels*zoom inside a scrollable pane), never a CSS transform, so a zoomed picture stays scrollable to its edge; a zoom keeps the point the reader was looking at, restored on the next animation frame after React commits the new box; the wheel listener is attached NATIVELY with {passive:false} because React's own wheel listener is passive and a preventDefault inside it does nothing, which would let the browser's own Ctrl+wheel page zoom fire on top; a checkerboard shows PNG transparency; past 300% the picture is drawn pixelated; and the status line names the true dimensions, the size on disk, the format and the SOURCE PIXEL under the pointer with its colour, sampled through a 1x1 canvas so inspecting a large photograph never copies the picture into a second buffer. Client-only by design: bytes come from the harness's own remote.workspaceFiles.readAll (the same call the shipped preview makes for a bytes-complete document, which already resolves the path inside the conversation workspace, refuses a symlink out, requires a regular file and enforces the 32 MiB single-file cap on the HOST side), so this package ships NO route, NO host state and NO path policy of its own - its Node half is one no-op row whose only job is to put the browser bundle in the boot graph. It REPLACES the shipped preview's bare intrinsic-size image only for image addresses, by RANKING and never by disabling a row: the type registers in the `extension` band with the image suffixes while the shipped preview claims dsh-resource://file/** at `fallback`, and canOpen refuses anything that is not an image address, so every other file type keeps exactly the surface it had, the shipped preview stays mounted as the fallback, and the editor (which vetoes images outright) is untouched. No guide entry on purpose: a blank image is not a document the + control should offer. Nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track

dsh-audio.role: WAV/RIFF (RF64 included), AIFF/AIFC and FLAC as a WAVEFORM (row `audio`, tab kind `audio`): one TRACK per channel, each a ROW of its own drawn full width with the gutter cell beside it of EXACTLY that row's height (L/R for a stereo pair, numbers past that, NO letter at all for mono - a lone M is a letter the reader has to decode), and a track height the reader drags from any row's bottom edge: ONE shared height for every track, 24px to 420px, because a waveform is read across tracks and separately sized tracks would no longer line up; an adaptive time ruler whose label widths are MEASURED, the min/max envelope with the RMS band drawn inside it, a linear or dBFS amplitude scale and an amplitude gain on Shift+wheel with NO button (the toolbar counts tracks instead), zoom by pxPerSecond from 1 to 500000 with the samples themselves drawn as stems once they are big enough, drag-to-select with the selection's peak and RMS reported while NAMING where they came from, and playback with the playhead driven by the AUDIO CLOCK rather than a CSS animation. The zoom moves the LAYOUT (the spacer is the file's duration times the zoom, so panning is the pane's own scrollLeft) and the canvas is VIEWPORT-ANCHORED (position:sticky;left:0) because a canvas cannot be 300000px wide - the layout is the file, the canvas is the window onto it, repainting on scroll; the wheel listener is native and non-passive (Ctrl/Cmd zooms at the pointer, Shift gains, a bare wheel scrolls sideways). CLIENT-ONLY like dsh-image: bytes come from the harness's own workspaceFiles remote, so there is no route, no host state and no path policy of its own and lib/index.js is one no-op row. THE WINDOW READ IS THE DESIGN: WAV/AIFF are decoded HERE one 2 MiB readBytes window at a time (a refusal carries details.limit, so the window is halved and asked for again), the samples are folded into a PEAK PYRAMID and dropped - level 0 one bucket per 256 samples of (min,max,rms) per channel, each level above grouping exactly four buckets of the one below, so a decimated RMS is the root of the mean of its children's squares - which is what lets a file far past the 32 MiB single-read cap still draw at a bounded memory cost; FLAC is decoded by the BROWSER (decodeAudioData), bounded by that cap, with its STREAMINFO parsed here first so even an undecodable-large FLAC states its exact rate, channels, bit depth and length, and the decoder is given a context at the FILE's own sample rate so a 44.1 kHz file is not silently resampled. An unsupported codec is refused BY NAME (IMA ADPCM, MACE, GSM, ima4), a truncated file draws what exists and says the tail is UNKNOWN rather than silence, and MP3/M4A/Ogg are deliberately NOT claimed (the shipped preview's own <audio> element still plays them). ALPHA.2 repaired four defects the four surfaces are pinned by the tracked check for: a fmt chunk whose block align is narrower than one frame is refused BY NAME rather than believed (the decoder walks the file's own stride, so believing it read each channel out of the NEXT frame's bytes - wrong samples, undefined for 8-bit, a raw DataView RangeError on a float file); a zero-size chunk (legal, exactly 8 bytes of header) is stepped OVER instead of ENDING the RIFF/IFF walk, which used to make any file carrying one unreadable; a prefix that is the WHOLE file is answered with the parser's own verdict rather than with the 8 MiB ceiling sentence, because the probe now passes the host's own eof (and a known size it has covered) down - a 20-byte RIFF...WAVE used to claim a header larger than the ceiling; and the canvas palette is ONE accent split by alpha into the four surfaces it paints (envelope 55%, RMS core solid, selection 16%, edge 50%), because the token path read a name the pinned line does not define and handed the SAME opaque colour to all four - so the RMS core was painted in its envelope's own colour and could not be seen, the stems were solid and the selection covered the waveform. It REPLACES the shipped bare audio element by RANKING - extension band with the three families' suffixes and a canOpen that refuses anything else - never by disabling a row, and adds NO guide entry. exports.__internals exposes the bundle's pure half so check-client-bundles.mjs can build its own WAV/AIFF/FLAC byte by byte and assert the decoded numbers, the windowed-decode-equals-whole-file claim included. No fork, no core row disabled, no npm dependency, no vendored engine, nothing for sync-vendored.ps1 to track
uses: @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-workspace-files (the workspaceFiles remote: readBytes windows, readAll, stat)

dsh-media.role: the pack's MEDIA ENGINE, host-only and deliberately unglamorous: three agent tools, two bundled skills, one pinned copy of ffmpeg, and the routes the dsh-video tab lives on - so the model and the interface cannot disagree about a file. THE TOOLS (lib/tools.js): media_probe describes any image, video or audio file from ffprobe's own reading of its header (container, duration, bitrate; per stream the codec, the exact pixel size and display aspect, the frame rate as BOTH its rational 30000/1001 and its decimal, pixel format and bit depth, rotation, sample rate, channel layout, language/title tags, and every chapter) and ends with the verdict a viewer needs - playable / image / remux / transcode - plus the exact ffmpeg command that would fix the last two, which is how an agent can look at a PNG at all (the read tool refuses binary files); media_run runs a REAL ffmpeg or ffprobe command as an ARGV ARRAY, never a shell string, so a path with a space, a filter graph and a literal & all arrive as themselves - it injects -hide_banner, -loglevel warning, -nostdin and -n (never overwrite) unless the caller sets a log level or asks for overwrite:true (which becomes -y), runs in the conversation workspace by default, kills at a deadline (120 s default, 600 s max), caps the output keeping head and tail and naming how much it dropped, and reports the exit code, the elapsed time and the files ffmpeg's own log named as outputs; media_frames pulls frames out at named timestamps, samples N evenly across the file, or tiles ONE contact sheet, writing CREATE-EXCLUSIVELY and reporting each file's REAL dimensions read back out of its own PNG/JPEG header. THE PIN (lib/binaries.json + lib/ffmpeg.js): the repository ships NO binary - a static ffmpeg is 130-170 MB per platform and would be multiplied into every clone, distribution and CI cache, and a committed Windows build helps nobody on macOS - so it ships a PIN instead: per platform and architecture the exact official static build URL and its SHA-256, downloaded ONCE on first need into $DSH_HOME/dsh-media/bin/<platform>-<arch>/ and verified against that hash BEFORE anything is executed, unpacked with the host's own tar, copied in through a .partial name and a rename so a binary that exists is a complete binary, and remembered by an install.json stamp. Resolution order: $DSH_MEDIA_FFMPEG/$DSH_MEDIA_FFPROBE, then a PATH install (the machine's own ffmpeg is used rather than a second copy being downloaded), then the provisioned copy, then nothing - and a tool call with nothing answers IMMEDIATELY, starting the pinned download in the background rather than blocking a turn on 170 MB (DSH_MEDIA_NO_INSTALL=1 disables that). A hash that does not match installs nothing, leaves no stamp, and says which two hashes disagreed; a platform this release pins nothing for (darwin-arm64, deliberately - no Apple-Silicon build publishes both a versioned URL and a checksum) is told so in a sentence naming the package managers instead of guessing at a download. tools/binaries.mjs is the maintainer's refresher (--check offline, --update from BtbN's own release digests plus a real hash of evermeet's macOS zips, --verify downloading every pinned archive and comparing); the `tools` folder is kept out of a distribution by the pack's own `skipdir tools` rule, so the refresher never ships. THE ROUTES (dsh-media/lib/index.js, SEVEN of them): GET /state and /health answer one capability snapshot (which binary answered and from where, the provisioned copy's state and progress, the caps, the tools, the skills); POST /provision starts or joins the pinned download; GET /report answers the same probe summary as JSON for the video tab, degrading to {ok:true,unavailable:true} when the host has no ffprobe - a fact about the machine, not a bad request; GET /file streams a media file WITH HTTP RANGE SUPPORT (206 + Content-Range + Accept-Ranges, suffix ranges, 416 on an unsatisfiable one, HEAD with no body) so a 2 GB film seeks instead of being read into memory, and serves this package's own cached conversions by KEY (`?cache=<32-hex>`, a caller never names a cache path); POST /remux starts or JOINS the background remux/transcode that makes a file browser-playable - the job id IS the content key (sha256 of realpath+size+mtime+mode), so asking twice joins the first, a finished copy is answered from the cache, and ffmpeg's own `-progress pipe:1` out_time_us drives the percentage rather than an estimate; GET /job reports it, and a partial file left by a failed conversion is never served. `/file` accepts only the video extensions the dsh-video tab claims (audio formats belong to dsh-audio's waveform and the shipped preview's player), re-validating the path exactly as the tools do: a session-relative path resolves inside that conversation's workspace with realpath on both sides (a symlink out is refused), an absolute path is read as given, and the target must be a regular file. TWO SKILLS (skills/ffmpeg-cli, skills/ffprobe-cli) are registered at runtime from the package folder AND copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers, teaching the argv-array interface, the injected guardrails, the container/codec choices a browser plays, trimming, frames, filters, concatenation and quality tradeoffs (ffmpeg), and the JSON/selected-field invocations, what each field family means, r_frame_rate vs avg_frame_rate, when -count_frames is worth its cost, and how to diagnose a file from its header alone (ffprobe). ALPHA.2 makes each bundled skill's runtime registration name ITS SOURCE BUCKET AND THE FILE IT READ, and the first half is a BUG FIX: `ctx.skills.get()` - which is what the `skill` tool calls to LOAD a skill, not just list it - runs the registry's own definition validator, and that validator requires a STRING `source`. A runtime registration never had one, so wherever this entry is the winning one (a host-scoped read, or a composition whose preset mounts no filesystem provider) both bundled skills answered `loaded skill 'x' source must be a string` and could not be loaded at all. The second half is `path` (this package's own `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) plus the folder as resourceBase, so the definition is file-backed and a skills browser can show and edit the document the model is given. `source` is prompt-visible metadata only - a runtime entry's precedence is its own rank (250) - so a preset's `$DSH_HOME/skills` copy still wins wherever the filesystem provider is mounted, and that copy is the watched, live-editable one. ALPHA.3 is the documentation half of the same promise, and it is where the examples stopped being decorative: each skill now has the references its summary routes to (filters.md for filter graphs, platforms.md for the parts that genuinely differ per host - measured, including the drive colon a Windows FILTER value needs two backslashes for and the drawtext crash the one-backslash form produces - failures.md for the message catalogue, which had grown a copy in two places, and the existing cookbook.md as the recipe book), and every example in all of them is SHAPED and then really RUN by scripts/checks/check-media-examples.mjs, which builds its own fixture set with real ffmpeg under the very names the documents read (clip.mp4, two.mkv, withsubs.mkv, attached.mkv, a.mp4/b.mp4/pal.png/list.txt/subs.srt, rotated.mp4, a genuinely interlaced interlaced.mp4 that probes field_order=tt, hdr.mp4, clip.ts and a variable-rate vfr.mp4), reads THIS build's own -encoders and -filters first so an example needing what the build lacks is skipped BY NAME rather than failed, and prints every skip with its reason instead of counting one as a pass. It exists because the check that looked like it covered examples iterated an EMPTY list - not one example in either skill is fenced json - so the arrays an agent is told to copy into media_run had never been verified, and nine of them turned out to be unusable, with prose welded onto the end of the array. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for scripts/sync-vendored.ps1 to track
uses: the host's own `tar` for unpacking a pinned archive
optional (only when provisioning): the pinned static builds from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds and evermeet.cx
vendors: NOT a vendored engine: lib/binaries.json is a PIN (URL + SHA-256 per platform-arch), and the bytes it names are downloaded to $DSH_HOME/dsh-media/bin only when a machine has no ffmpeg of its own. Provenance: BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds autobuild-2026-09-26-13-03 (LGPL static, win32/linux x64+arm64) and evermeet.cx 9.0.2 (GPL, darwin-x64) - the Windows archive's hash was verified by downloading it (173535440 bytes, matching the digest GitHub publishes for the asset)

dsh-video.role: VIDEO as a surface that actually plays (row `video`, tab kind `video`): MP4, M4V, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI, WMV, FLV, OGV, MPEG-TS and 3GP open in a player that FITS the pane (a real layout size - `max-width/max-height:100%` - never a scale transform, so a 4K film is whole and a phone clip is not smeared across the pane), with a 38px top bar carrying the file's name, duration, pixel size and size on disk, a chapter jump, -5s/+5s buttons, a Facts toggle and the conversion action when the file needs one. CLIENT-ONLY ON PURPOSE: the bytes, the probe and the ffmpeg all belong to dsh-media (row `media`), which owns the Range-capable /api/dsh-media/file route, /report and the remux/transcode job - ffmpeg has one owner in this pack, and a second implementation of the media path policy would be a second thing to get wrong. So this package ships NO route, NO host state and NO path policy of its own: lib/index.js is one no-op row whose only job is to put the browser bundle in the boot graph, exactly like dsh-image and dsh-audio. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE is that the <video> element is handed a URL, never bytes: no arrayBuffer, no blob, no workspaceFiles read - the host route speaks HTTP Range, so the browser streams AND seeks, which reading a 2 GB film into memory could never do. It claims BOTH address shapes: the ordinary dsh-resource://file/session/<id>/<path> a Files-tab click produces, and dsh-resource://file/absolute/<path>, which is reassembled in the three cases that matter (a Windows drive carries its own root, a UNC path keeps an empty first segment and needs its slash back, a POSIX path lost its leading slash) because getting any of them wrong points the tab at another FILE. The tab type is `extension`-band with the video suffixes and a canOpen that refuses anything else, so it REPLACES the shipped preview's own <video> element by RANKING (extension 3 beats the shipped text type's fallback 1) and never by disabling a core row; audio formats are deliberately NOT claimed - WAV/AIFF/FLAC are dsh-audio's waveform and MP3/M4A/Ogg are the shipped preview's player, so claiming them would take a surface away rather than add one; there is deliberately NO guide entry. THE FACTS PANEL is dsh-media's probe rendered as a drawer: container, duration, bitrate, size, one block per stream (codec/profile, pixel size and display aspect, frame rate with its exact rational, pixel format and bit depth, sample rate and channel layout, bitrate, frame count, language, title, default/forced), every chapter as a JUMP TARGET (a click seeks and plays), the file's tags, and the browser verdict with the exact ffmpeg command that would fix a remux/transcode, copyable. A FILE THE BROWSER CANNOT PLAY is where the tab earns its place: the toolbar and the play-error overlay offer the ONE action that fixes it - `Remux to MP4` (instant, no re-encoding) or `Convert for the browser` (H.264/AAC) - POSTed to dsh-media, polled every 700 ms with ffmpeg's own percentage on a thin progress bar, and the finished cached MP4 is then played through the same file route (?cache=<key>), so a second visit to that file is instant. The poll is keyed on the job's ID and whether it runs, never on the job OBJECT (every poll replaces it, and an effect depending on it would restart its own timer on every tick). NOTHING IS EVER A DEAD END: `No ffmpeg on this machine yet` offers the pinned download (POST /provision, then a re-probe) with the message naming what will be fetched; `ffprobe could not read this file` and a host error keep the player on screen behind the notice with `Play it anyway` (the browser decodes plenty ffprobe cannot describe) and `Read it again`; and a profile that installed this bundle WITHOUT dsh-media gets one sentence naming the package that owns /api/dsh-media/*. No fork, no core row disabled, nothing for scripts/sync-vendored.ps1 to track
uses: dsh-rightbar (the tab registry and the keyed pane seats)
dsh-media (the file/report/remux/job routes and the ffmpeg behind them - resolved over HTTP, so a profile without it still loads and says so)

dsh-browser.role: the pack's own BROWSER, and the replacement for the shipped Browser tab. The shipped one is an `<iframe src=...>` with a six-line host half (`function apply() {}`) and no proxy or route at all, so a site's own framing policy decided whether anything appeared: measured from this machine, google.com answers `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, github.com answers `deny` plus `frame-ancestors 'none'`, developer.mozilla.org answers `DENY` and news.ycombinator.com answers `DENY` plus `frame-ancestors 'self'`, so the frame showed "www.google.com refused to connect" - while example.com and en.wikipedia.org, which send neither header, loaded fine. This package's row disables that one (the disable stays with the package that replaces the row, as dsh-rightbar does for the bar) and renders the page on the HOST instead, so the site's framing policy cannot decide anything and no remote code runs in the user's browser or in this session's origin. THE PIPELINE is one function (`runRender`) shared by the three tools the model calls and by the routes the tab posts to, so what a person sees and what the model was told cannot drift. `lib/policy.js` is the pure half: https only, port 443 only, no credentials in a URL, no IP-literal hosts, a qualified public hostname (two or more labels, so `localhost` and `intranet` are refused before anything resolves), an optional allow/block list, and a public-unicast-only address classifier (v4 private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/benchmark/multicast/reserved/metadata plus v6 `::`, `::1`, ULA, link-local, multicast, 6to4, Teredo, NAT64 and IPv4-mapped forms classified by the address they embed) that refuses the WHOLE answer set when any address in it is not public - the harness's own `web-fetch-http` rule, applied where a browser can be made to obey it. `lib/gate.js` is the egress gate: a loopback `CONNECT`-only proxy the engine is launched with (`--proxy-server`, plus `<-loopback>` to remove Chrome's implicit loopback bypass and `--host-resolver-rules="MAP * ~NOTFOUND, EXCLUDE 127.0.0.1"`), which resolves every destination itself, refuses the set unless every answer is public, connects to the address it validated so a second lookup cannot rebind the name, bounds every tunnel (idle timeout, byte cap, tunnel ceiling) and RECORDS every decision - so the tab's policy panel and a tool result can state what the engine actually reached instead of asserting that it was safe. Proxy authentication is answered by the host over CDP (`Fetch.authRequired`), so the credential never travels in a URL. `lib/engine.js` runs the machine's own Chrome/Chromium/Edge (never a bundled one: `DSH_BROWSER_ENGINE`, then the per-OS install locations, then PATH) in a FRESH throwaway profile per render, headless, extensionless, sync-less, with no `--no-sandbox`, no `--disable-web-security` and no `--ignore-certificate-errors`, driven over the DevTools Protocol through Node's global `WebSocket` (no dependency added), and it kills the BROWSER process CDP reports rather than the launcher Chrome exits at once on Windows, then deletes the profile. It navigates, settles, screenshots the viewport or the whole page (pixel-capped, and it says when a capture was cut) and measures: `Runtime.evaluate` for the page's own numbers and its text, and a selector walker for `box`, computed `style`, `text`, `attrs` and `html` per CSS selector - the design/dimension tool. The PNG's pixel size is read back out of the file's own IHDR chunk, never from what was asked for. THREE TOOLS: `browser_render` (a picture plus the page's numbers, the gate's verdict and the page's own destinations), `browser_query` (measured geometry and computed styles) and `browser_text` (the post-script text with its link inventory) - each labelling page content as DATA that must never be followed as guidance, and each carrying a conversation card with the screenshot and a button that opens the tab at that URL. ONE BUNDLED SKILL (`web-render`) teaches when to render instead of `web_fetch`, how to read a measurement, and what the policy refuses. THE TAB (`lib/client.js`, hand-written, no build step) keeps the REPLACED package's id and kind so persisted Browser tabs resolve here, and draws four views from one render: Visual (the PNG on a zoom ladder that moves the LAYOUT box, never a CSS transform, with fit and 100%), Reader (the post-script text with clickable links re-gated through the same policy), Metrics (viewport, content size, counts, timing, page requests) and Policy (the engine, the gate's tunnels/challenges/refusals by name, and the fact that an extra host in the allow list is the ENGINE's own connectivity probe - evidence the gate is the only way out). It has viewport presets, full-page and dark toggles, its own back/forward over render history, a per-tab state map so two Browser tabs do not share an address bar, a request token so a slow render cannot paint over a newer one, and a permanent banner saying the picture is a host render and not a live page. THE INTERACTIVE LIVE MODE IS PARKED and refuses in a sentence (`LIVE_PARKED`): a live frame is the one thing that would put a remote page back inside this session's origin, which is what this package exists to avoid. `scripts/checks/check-browser-node.mjs` is the tracked check: the policy table, the engine argv guards (headless, throwaway profile, the gate as the only proxy, the loopback bypass removed, the resolver-rule exclusion, and the absence of every disarming flag), the PNG header reader, the gate's refusals by rule plus its credential challenge and its trace, the row's three tools/routes/viewport clamping/artifact id, the image route's refusal of a crafted id - and a LIVE half that skips loudly without an engine or the internet and otherwise renders example.com for real, asserting the PNG's header size, the gate's tunnels and challenges, that the PAGE only ever talked to the rendered host, a measured selector's box and computed styles, the post-script text, a real TLS round trip through the gate and the byte cap cutting an oversized tunnel. No `sync-vendored.ps1` involvement (nothing forked), no npm dependency, and NO PATH POLICY at all: the package reads and writes no caller-supplied path, only its own artifacts under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-browser/`. SHIPPED AND TURNED OFF (the master layer disables the `browser` row, and it is installed last so it wins): a profile loads no Browser tab, no `/api/dsh-browser/*` routes, no `browser_render` / `browser_query` / `browser_text` and no client bundle, so the engine, the egress path and the three tools hold no surface at all until someone deletes those two lines from packages/dsh-vn-master/cordis.patch.yml; the package, its checks and this entry stay in step, so re-enabling it is a one-line decision rather than a reconstruction.

dsh-diagrams.role: Mermaid and TikZ diagrams as a surface of their own: six tools (diagram_write/patch/read/verify/publish/delete) whose every write is VALIDATED before it is stored - Mermaid by parsing it headlessly with the SAME vendored engine the browser renders with (a child process, a DOM stub and vm, so the stub never touches the host process), TikZ by compiling it with the machine's own TeX engine under -no-shell-escape, MIKTEX_AUTOINSTALL=0 and openin_any/openout_any=p in a private temp folder - so a broken diagram comes back to the model as the parser's/compiler's own line-accurate error instead of a blank picture, plus ADVISORY lint findings (a picture with nodes and no edges, more nodes than a reader takes in, an unclosed-looking label, a TikZ document that compiled to no picture or to several pages) that never change the status, and two degenerate sources refused in plain words (empty/comments-only, and a TikZ document with no drawing command in it). NOTHING THE ENGINE BUILDS CAN REACH THE PAGE (alpha.3): mermaid is parsed FIRST and rendered with suppressErrorRendering: true into a container the plugin owns, because render(id, source) with no container builds #d<id> on document.body and removes it only on SUCCESS - so every failed render used to leave behind a 2412x512 'Syntax error in text / mermaid version 11.17.2' picture in the interface, one per failure. The browser also REPORTS what it drew (POST /render-report, stored per revision, read back as drawn/stale/failed/pending through diagram_read), which is the one verdict the host cannot produce alone: parsing proves the source is valid, only a renderer proves the picture exists. diagram_verify re-runs the whole validation without writing or bumping the revision. two bundled skills (mermaid-diagrams, tikz-diagrams) authored in skills/ and copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by the installer; per-conversation state in ONE file under $DSH_HOME/dsh-diagrams/sessions (never a session event: dsh-session-persistence refuses a log containing a type outside KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES without the ignorable marker, which Session.append() cannot set) plus a content-addressed artifact cache; and, in the right bar, one tab per diagram (dsh-resource://diagram/session/<session>/<id>) with a source drawer, zoom controls (25%-400% over a picture laid out at 80% of the pane, as the 100% rung) and an export menu that SAVES EVERY FORMAT TO THE HOST'S DESKTOP (mmd/md/tex/pdf/svg/png, create-exclusively, the same deal the screenshot control makes) beside an index page (sidebar://diagrams) whose guide entry (order 40) is what + / Start lists. Every tool call renders its diagram inline in the conversation with a link that opens its tab, and the state route carries the SOURCE and the REVISION the browser needs to draw and to report against. TeX is optional: without an engine a TikZ diagram is still stored and exported as .tex, and every surface says so. No fork, no core row disabled, no npm dependency, no network - the Connection fetch registry takes EXACT routes and GET/HEAD/POST only, which is why the vendored engine is one self-contained file on one route and every write is a POST. ALPHA.4 makes the surfaces usable and the verdicts objective: the diagram tab lays a picture out at 80% of the pane and adds a zoom ladder (25%-400%) with DRAG TO PAN: the ladder moves the BOX rather than applying a transform, so a zoomed diagram stays scrollable to its edge, a zoomed box STRETCHES its children (a column flex container sizes children to their content, so without that rule the box zoomed while the diagram did not), panning is the canvas own scrollLeft/scrollTop with the grab cursor measured from real overflow, and a zoom keeps the point the reader was looking at; every export (mmd/md/tex/pdf/svg/png) is SAVED TO THE DESKTOP of the machine running the harness by a new authenticated route that resolves the Desktop per request (OneDrive-redirected Windows, XDG on Linux, the home folder last), writes create-exclusively under the diagram's own name and answers with the ABSOLUTE path the panel reports - the conversation folder is never written to, and the browser download survives only as the fallback for a profile without that row; the browser verdict is now ONE function in lib/store.js used by the tool result, the state route and the tab pill, with four objective states (drawn / failed / stale / pending) that carry BOTH revision numbers and an explicit `reported` field, so a report about an older revision can never read as this revision's picture, and the verdict OMITS its error/at keys rather than nulling them - with `error: undefined` on a drawn verdict the tool registry's JSON-round-trip rule rejected the output, so EVERY diagram the browser had rendered came back to the model as 'value is not lossless JSON'; a cache hit re-reads the verdict the compile was cached WITH instead of assuming ok (a failed compile that still produced a picture was being reported as fine on the second call); the conversation's total diagram source is budgeted (4 MiB, checked on write AND patch, replacing a diagram charged once) so the per-conversation state file can no longer be pushed past the size at which the store reads it as empty and every diagram in the conversation disappears at once; Mermaid validations run through a bounded child pool (2 at a time, bounded queue) instead of an unbounded fan-out of 3.5 MB engine children; the DOM stub now exposes window.CSS, without which the engine's sequence-diagram box parser died on a `new Option()` fallback and EVERY `box` diagram came back 'stored but not validated'; and each bundled skill gains a reference/complex-diagrams.md - full worked sources, budgets, layout recipes and failure modes - for diagrams too big for the syntax summary in SKILL.md, and the tracked checks keep those examples honest (check-skill-examples.mjs parses or compiles every fenced example with the plugin's own engines, and node-routes now validates every tool result against the schema the tool DECLARES, the gap that let a `reported: null` against `type: integer` ship and refuse every fresh write). ALPHA.6 adds the LIBRARY: a diagram used to belong to the conversation that drew it and to nothing else, so there is now a second scope - ONE file for the whole harness ($DSH_HOME/dsh-diagrams/library.json) written by the same store class with a fixed name instead of a name per conversation - and `diagram_write { scope: library }` writes straight into it while a new tool `diagram_publish { id }` copies a conversation diagram in (one call, no source round-trip, an id already there is replaced and the copy is re-validated through the content-addressed cache). Every read resolves a BARE ID IN THE LIBRARY FIRST and then in the conversation, so diagram_read { id: 'jepa-model' } finds the shared diagram from a chat that never saw it written and says which scope it found it in; the address dsh-resource://diagram/library/<id> names NO conversation, which is what makes a citation durable across chats and lets the one `diagram` tab type claim that address shape too; the index page shows both halves library-first, the state route carries the library with every conversation's diagrams (so the client needs no second store), and the artifact, export, diagram and render-report routes all take a scope. Two details carry the weight: a panel edit writes back where the diagram ALREADY is (without that, editing a library diagram in its tab would quietly create a conversation-only second copy), and deleting a diagram no longer drops its cached artifact blindly, because the cache is content-addressed and shared - an identical diagram elsewhere is the same file. ALPHA.7 makes each bundled skill's runtime registration name ITS SOURCE BUCKET AND THE FILE IT READ, for the reasons dsh-media records in full: `ctx.skills.get()` (what the `skill` tool calls to LOAD a skill) requires a STRING `source` in the definition it validates, so a runtime registration without one is unloadable wherever it wins - a latent bug, not a cosmetic one - and `path` (this package's own `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) is what makes the definition file-backed so a skills browser can show and edit it. A runtime entry's precedence is its own rank (250), so a preset's `$DSH_HOME/skills` copy still wins wherever the filesystem provider is mounted
uses: a TeX engine on PATH (pdflatex/xelatex/lualatex) for TikZ
vendors: the two skills copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers

dsh-pdf.role: PDF the agent can actually READ and SCAN, plus a real PDF reader and a PDF index in the right bar. FIVE tools - pdf_info (pages, sizes, metadata, outline, attachments, forms/signatures, encryption, and per page whether there is a TEXT LAYER at all), pdf_read (a page range in plain reading order or in a geometric LAYOUT reconstruction that keeps columns and label/value pairs apart), pdf_find (literal or regex with page, line and context), pdf_render (page pictures through the host's own rasterizer, written as new PNGs) and pdf_scan (the SCANNER: recognize the pages that are a picture of text) - over a VENDORED pdf.js 6.3.289, the exact build the harness's own preview inlines, run in a CHILD process with argv only, a 25 s deadline, --max-old-space-size=512 and an 8 MiB output cap, and gated inside with isEvalSupported:false (a PDF's embedded JavaScript is never evaluated), useWorkerFetch:false with no URL fetching anywhere, enableXfa:false, useSystemFonts:false and the vendored cMap/standard-font/wasm trees as file:// URLs - so a corrupt or hostile document is a reported failure and never a wedged host. Identity is CONTENT: the SHA-256 of the bytes names the cache entry under $DSH_HOME/dsh-pdf/artifacts, so an edited file can never serve a stale answer; index.json holds the document facts, stats.json the per-page numbers merged as pages arrive, pages/<n>.json one page's text in both modes, images/<n>@<dpi>dpi.png a kept raster and ocr/<n>.<lang>@<dpi>dpi.p<psm>.txt a recognition named by every input that can change it, all atomic and LRU-pruned at 512 MiB. THE SCANNER is one pipeline shared by the pdf_scan tool and by the reader's own 'scan this page' action through POST /api/dsh-pdf/scan: with no `pages` it selects exactly the pages pdf_info found to have NO text layer - never OCRing a page whose real text could be read instead - validates the language against the engine's own --list-langs BEFORE drawing anything, and turns every absence (no rasterizer, no OCR engine, no language data, no page needing a scan) into a sentence naming what to install or do. THE TAB TYPE is `pdf`, band `extension`, patterns ['*.pdf']: it REPLACES the shipped preview's bare PDF renderer by RANKING (extension 3 beats the shipped text type's fallback 1) while canOpen refuses anything that is not a .pdf, so every other file type keeps the surface it had, the shipped preview stays mounted as the fallback, and NO core row is disabled. TWO address shapes: the ordinary dsh-resource://file/session/<id>/<path>, and this package's own dsh-resource://pdf/absolute/<whole-path-encoded> for a document outside any workspace (a chat attachment under $DSH_HOME/attachments/v1/files/... or a file in Downloads), because the ordinary grammar drops the leading slash of a POSIX absolute path and would silently point elsewhere. The READER has a zoom ladder plus fit width/fit page (zoom moves the LAYOUT, never a CSS transform, so a zoomed page stays scrollable to its edge), page navigation by button, field and keyboard, rotation, pdf.js's own TextLayer (positioned against --total-scale-factor, the variable pdf.js 6 reads) for selection and copy, in-document search with hit count and next/previous that highlights inside the rendered text layer without moving a glyph, drag-to-pan measured from real overflow, and honest failures (a damaged file, a locked document with a password prompt held in memory and never stored, an engine that will not start) each with a Retry; every page with no text layer says so and offers a one-click SCAN whose recognized text appears under the page, labelled a TRANSCRIPTION with the engine, language and resolution it came from. alpha.3 adds the SIDE PANEL: a lazily drawn THUMBNAIL RAIL (IntersectionObserver rooted on the rail itself, so a thumbnail two screens down never draws until it is nearly shown; capped at 300 pages, and the rail says so) and the document's OWN BOOKMARK OUTLINE, resolved in the browser through getOutline/getDestination/getPageIndex, bounded to 200 entries and 4 levels, with an unresolvable bookmark kept as information rather than dropped - plus a SECOND PAGE TYPE `pdfs` (address sidebar://pdfs, priority builtin, NO patterns, guide entry at order 50 after Files 10 / Editor 20 / History 30 / Diagrams 40) whose body lists every PDF in the conversation's workspace with size, mtime and an opt-in page count, and opens one through the ordinary openResource action so the registry decides what claims it. The index is backed by GET /api/dsh-pdf/list, a timid bounded walk (depth 6, 200 files, a skip-list of node_modules/.git/__pycache__/.venv/..., symlinks not followed, .pdf only) that reports page counts only when asked and only for 12 documents - a count means parsing, which is worth 12 files on a click and never worth doing for a directory nobody asked about. The wasm image decoders (JBIG2, OpenJPEG, qcms; 13 files, 1.5 MB) are vendored and served as ONE base64 map by the same custom BinaryDataFactory, because without them a scanned page draws blank while looking like a document. The engine is NOT in the bundle - the harness reads every client bundle at boot and pdf.js is 1.8 MB - so engine, worker and assets are fetched from this plugin's own authenticated routes and the engine is imported from a blob URL. TEN route registrations (five named handlers plus the five fixed vendor assets), all EXACT paths because the connection's fetch registry matches exact paths only: GET state|health (capabilities including the OCR language list, cache facts, vendored version, caps), GET file (the bytes the tab reads, with the content hash as x-dsh-pdf-sha256), GET list (the workspace index), POST scan (the reader's scan, same pipeline as the tool; a capability refusal answers 200 with {ok:false,reason,message}), and /vendor/{pdf.min.mjs,pdf.worker.min.mjs,cmaps.json,standard-fonts.json,wasm.json}. READ-ONLY: no tool modifies, merges, splits, rotates, fills or signs a PDF, and pdf_render only ever writes NEW files, create-exclusively, under a name the plugin generates (a caller names a DIRECTORY, never a file). Path policy is stated rather than implied: a session-relative path is realpath-checked to stay inside the conversation workspace (a symlink out is refused, not followed) while an absolute path is read directly, and either way the target must be a regular .pdf within the ceiling (512 MiB for the tools, 256 MiB for the tab). There is now NO byte cache in the browser half at all: loadDocumentBytes reads /api/dsh-pdf/file again for every open and owns exactly one buffer, a body that comes back short (the file changed mid-read) or empty is refused in its own words instead of pdf.js's 'not a readable PDF', and the loading task - which owns the worker and the parsed document - is destroyed when the tab unmounts, when the address changes, or when Retry replaces it, because a task left alone leaked one worker thread per open. Pinned from both sides: check-pdf-node.mjs drives the vendored engine with ONE array twice (the second hand-off must FAIL - a DataCloneError in Node, the postMessage line above in a browser) and with two FRESH arrays, and check-client-bundles.mjs fails if the byte cache or the teardown goes. alpha.6 fixes the READER'S FIT, and the reason a page drifted right when a panel was resized: an undrawn page reserved minWidth 45vw / minHeight 60vh - units of the WINDOW - inside a reader that is one pane of a dock, and because .dpf-pages is min-width:min-content a single placeholder wider than the pane stretched the whole column past it, so every page was centred in a box wider than the pane: the page slid right, its left margin became a visible gap and its right edge left the pane (measured in Chrome against the bundle's own dress: a 44px gap with the right edge clipped at a 700px pane in a 1600px window, 246px / -197px at 2500px, and worse the wider the window). dsh-canvas.role: CANVAS: a design page the agent drives, and the first surface in the chat panel's own view ring (the conversation.view entry with the id `canvas` at order 20 - Chat is 0 and Trajectory is 10, so it sits to the right of Trajectory, and unlike Trajectory it is not gated on the developer-tools setting). Two facts about that ring were read out of the pinned bundles rather than assumed: only the ACTIVE view is mounted, and a conversation view receives no sessionId prop - it learns its session from its own inject(sessionId) face. The view becomes full height with the composer floating over it through data-conversation-composer-overlay. TEN tools own the surface - canvas_new (a starter from a destination preset, an optional archetype and an optional STYLE), canvas_write, canvas_patch (pointer ops set/remove/insert, so moving one element never costs a whole document), canvas_read, canvas_style (apply a LOOK from the style library to an existing design - palette, type behaviour, shape language, surface and art - and it never moves anything), canvas_publish (conversation -> a harness-wide library, bare ids resolving library-first), canvas_delete, canvas_render, canvas_export and canvas_assets. THE STYLE LIBRARY IS THE OTHER HALF OF A DESIGN, AND IT IS DATA: lib/styles/.json holds a look (palette roles, type behaviour, shape language, surface, art treatment, and rules.do / rules.dont / gates) and lib/styles/apply.js is ONE pure transform that applies it. Composition and look stay separate decisions - an archetype is WHICH design, a style is HOW it looks - so canvas_new takes a style and canvas_style re-styles a design that exists; the tab has a style picker beside the preset and a side-panel card carrying the current pack intent, rules and gates. APPLYING A STYLE NEVER MOVES ANYTHING: it replaces the colour roles and rewrites every colour LITERAL in the document that was one of the old role values (the only way to re-colour a canonical document, which carries literals everywhere), sets the type behaviour, and takes the radius/border/shadow/surface/art language from the pack, leaving geometry, layer count and every word untouched. The scale factor is applied as a DELTA against the style the document already carries (which is why a canonical document records its own style field), so applying the same style twice is a no-op and switching back restores the original type sizes exactly, and a pack cannot express what the language does not have (there is no blur, so glass is translucency plus a hairline plus a soft shadow, and its own intent says so). vendor/styles-doc.mjs GENERATES skills/canvas-design/reference/styles.md from the packs and --checks it, so the catalogue the model reads cannot drift from the library the host applies. THE DOCUMENT IS A SMALL JSON LANGUAGE validated on the host before it is stored: six node kinds (frame, text, image, shape, art, svg), a token block (colour / font / scale / space / radius), twenty-two typed refusals by code, and a CANONICAL form (tokens resolved, defaults filled, floats rounded) that canvas_read hands back, that a patch is applied against, and that therefore has to re-validate unchanged - a tracked assertion, because a {type:"solid"} paint (the canonical form of every colour) once failed its own validator and made every edit to a stored design impossible. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE IS THAT THE HOST CANNOT PAINT: a design is laid out with real text metrics, which only a browser has, and the PNG must come from the same code path that draws the artboard or "it looked right in the tab" becomes a bug class. So the host owns the document and the BROWSER owns the pixels, joined by a render queue: canvas_render enqueues a request carrying the document and its revision, the page long-polls GET /api/dsh-canvas/render-queue?session=* (page-level on purpose - a render asked for in one conversation is answered while another is on screen, because the request names its own session), paints, encodes the PNG plus a 25%-scale feed thumbnail (roughly a phone feed, which is how a banner is actually seen), computes the measurements and the lints, posts them back, and the tool resolves with a path the model reads with read_image. A failed render is a VERDICT, not a silence: drawn / failed / stale / pending per revision, the vocabulary dsh-diagrams proved, carried by the tool result, the rail's pill and the artboard. ONE LAYOUT, TWO PAINTERS: lib/engine.js is ONE file with ZERO static imports and no globals at module scope, because the browser fetches it from /api/dsh-canvas/vendor/engine.js and imports it from a blob URL (a blob-URL module resolves no relative specifiers - the constraint that made dsh-pdf's pdf.js and dsh-editor's CodeMirror single files). Its layout() is pure with the measurer INJECTED (the browser passes canvas.measureText plus fontBoundingBoxAscent/Descent; the tracked check passes a synthetic metrics table), and it emits ONE draw-op list that BOTH painters consume - the canvas painter is what the artboard draws AND what the PNG export rasterizes, so the export cannot disagree with the preview, and toSvg walks the same list for the vector output with images inlined as data URLs and a nested may not fetch anything. A frame's hug is on the axis its DIRECTION names - mixing them made a row frame as tall as its child was wide, found by instrumenting the function and now a regression assertion. THE FONTS ARE VENDORED: Inter (400/600/700) and Space Grotesk (500/700) as Latin WOFF2 subsets (96 KB, SIL OFL, licence texts committed), fetched and pinned by vendor/build.mjs (upstream URL + SHA-256 per file; --check runs offline and inside the tracked check), served from the plugin's own routes, loaded BEFORE the first layout (a face that has not loaded would re-wrap a headline with the fallback's metrics), reported as the families that actually resolved, and embedded as data URLs in an .svg export; `system` is the deliberate choice for the mono role. PRESETS ARE DATA with a verifiedOn date and sources - ten destinations (github-social 1280x640, github-readme, og, the three LinkedIn banners/posts, the 4:5 carousel page, x-post, poster-a3 at 300 dpi), each with its safe areas (safe guides and keep-out regions: LinkedIn's profile photograph, the company logo square, X's 1.91:1 crop), its margin, formats, byte ceiling and the click path where the file goes - because these numbers MOVE and a table with no provenance is one nobody can re-check. EIGHT ARCHETYPES are complete starter compositions shared by canvas_new and the tab's + New gallery. EXPORTS land on the Desktop by default or in the conversation folder on request, create-exclusively (-2, -3, ... nothing is overwritten), at 1x or 2x, with the preset deciding the format and the ceiling (an export over the ceiling still writes and SAYS it is over). ASSETS are the only images a design may name - a stored one (content-addressed by SHA-256, so importing the same picture twice costs one copy) or a workspace-relative path resolved on the host with realpath containment - and a REMOTE URL is deliberately not a thing a design can name, because it cannot be inlined into an SVG, it would leak a fetch from someone's browser and it would make the design irreproducible. State is per-conversation plus one library plus a content-addressed asset store under $DSH_HOME/dsh-canvas/, with write-enforced budgets (300 KB a document, 4 MB a conversation, 64 designs, 12 MB an asset, 256 assets) rather than a file that grows too large to load. TWO SKILLS carry the craft and the delivery rules - canvas-design (the loop, the whole document reference, every report code with a fix, the composition craft with numbers and twelve recipes) and social-banners (the per-destination table with the reason each safe area exists, the feed-reality test, @2x arithmetic, where each file is uploaded, and the honest note that the numbers move) - registered at runtime and copied into $DSH_HOME/skills by both installers. NOT here, deliberately: any image generation (pictures come from the workspace, a paste, or the ten seeded art generators), HTML/CSS (a design is JSON: nothing to sandbox, no external fetch, no headless browser in the export path), direct manipulation, more than one artboard per design, and an unattended host renderer (a render needs the app PAGE, not the tab, and says so in one sentence when nothing answers). scripts/checks/check-canvas-node.mjs drives the whole host half hermetically - the engine, both painters (the canvas one through a recorder), the store, the assets, the nine tools, every route, and the whole render round trip with a synthetic browser posting a real PNG back - inside a temp DSH_HOME; the browser half is asserted in check-client-bundles.mjs with the real React runtime; and check-skill-examples.mjs runs every ```canvas block in the shipped skills through the real validator and layout.
